She shouts, makes purposeless movements and thrashes in bed, sometimes with urinary incontinence.
Her family cannot easily wake her, and she cannot remember the events.

Her family has recorded night-time glucose around 2.0 mmol/L; inpatient night-time monitoring recorded 1.2–2.0 mmol/L.
She reports no history of diabetes.
She takes irbesartan for hypertension.
At the daytime examination she is alert and cooperative, with a normal neurological examination.
An electroencephalogram (EEG) showed no definite epileptiform discharges.
five days of low-grade fever and severe headache
Examination recorded marked meningeal signs; head CT showed no abnormality.
Initial cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) contained 183 cells/µL, 97.8% lymphocytes, and protein 83.3 mg/dL.
CSF PCR did not identify an infectious cause, and Borrelia serology was negative. No CSF culture result is supplied.
During that admission she received intravenous dexamethasone for nine days.
She improved and was discharged after 12 days on 11 March 2026.
Persistent headache and photophobia led to further emergency visits.
On 14 March she was readmitted with severe orthostatic headache, upper-limb tremor and dizziness.
Brain MRI was normal.
Repeat CSF contained 178 cells/µL, 97.7% lymphocytes, and protein 36.6 mg/dL.
watery diarrhoea three to four times daily for a year, with upper-abdominal discomfort and distal numbness.
Diarrhoea persisted.
Over the preceding six months he developed exertional breathlessness, fatigue and a 10 kg weight loss.
At the initial examination, blood pressure was 80/46 mmHg and heart rate 52 beats/min.
No updated vital signs are supplied for the later investigation-review point.
Echocardiography showed symmetric left-ventricular wall thickening, septal thickness 14.1 mm, LVEF 36%, grade-II diastolic dysfunction and relative apical sparing on strain.

Cardiac MRI showed diffuse wall thickening, high native myocardial T1, extracellular volume 49.85%–52.47%, and diffuse subendocardial late gadolinium enhancement involving the left ventricle and interatrial septum.
Serum/urine immunofixation and serum free-light-chain testing found no monoclonal gammopathy.
Alpha-galactosidase A activity was 1.70 µmol/L/h (laboratory reference >2.0); GLA sequencing found no pathogenic variant. Plasma lyso-Gb3 was not measured.
Technetium-PYP scintigraphy showed planar grade-1 myocardial uptake and a heart-to-contralateral-lung ratio >1.42; acquisition timing and additional technical details are not supplied here.
